what_it_covers: the machine side per OS: the daemon's own dial (quicdial.Dial + defaultQUICConfig on the OS UDP socket) sends one 200 MiB QUIC stream, through a 50 ms UDP delay line, into a receiver with the edge's receive windows (mirrored from edge/internal/datacarrier endpointQUICConfig: 256 KiB initial, 4 MiB maximum stream, 64 MiB connection). Median of three fresh connections must be >= 150 Mbit/s. The edge always runs on Linux and is proven end to end in cell L (e2e.yml throughput, 180-184 Mbit/s).
why_not_through_the_prod_edge: a hosted runner is 228-235 ms from both prod edges (India), real devices upload at ~18 Mbit/s from home; the coordinator accepted this check as the M and W tick (2026-11-16)
binaries: cross-compiled with go test -c from the committed tree (GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64, GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64) on hermes, run as plain test binaries

macos.machine: pbmac2 (macOS 26.6.2, 2 vCPU Tart VM on apple), fleet-mac2.lock held

windows.machine: victus (Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC, 12 logical CPUs)

fixture_lessons: Windows failed (96-140 Mbit/s, 49-176 lost packets in the sender's trace) until the delay relay's UDP sockets got 8 MiB buffers: the OS default (64 KB on Windows) dropped the relay's bursts. The 50 ms must be present at the handshake (a connection that measured ~1 ms first makes quic-go's HyStart leave slow start at once).
ran_on_runners: not yet on the GitHub-hosted Windows runner; its queue was hours long. cross-platform.yml runs the test on every push to main (Windows leg, no race).
